$source: Skyline — airline / travel-retail brand for the boxfusion.test flight booking app. Authored 2026-07-28 by shesha-claude-designer from the shesha default token contract (every key name preserved so roles.* resolves).
$description: Deep aviation blue (#0B4A8F) anchors every interactive affordance — the colour of an airline's own chrome, darker and cooler than Shesha Cobalt so it reads as travel rather than government. Warm amber (#F59E0B) is the single accent, reserved for money and attention: fares, pending payment, delayed flights. Surfaces are a cool off-white (#F5F7FA) so white boarding-pass cards lift off the page. Type is a cool near-black (#14202E), never pure black. Unlike Shesha, Skyline is elevation-forward: soft layered shadows and larger radii give the card-heavy booking screens depth, because a boarding pass is an object, not a table row.
$weightPolicy: Retains the 400/600 binary for body and headings. 500 is permitted ONLY for status-chip and micro-label text (cabin class, fare captions, IATA codes). Route codes and fares may use familyMono for tabular alignment.

accent.$use: sidebar + top-header chrome depth and the data-viz primary series only — never a general CTA colour (that is brand.primary). The warm amber accent this brand is known for lives in the semantic warning ramp (semantic.warningIcon #F59E0B) and the warning status tone, so it stays tied to money and attention rather than becoming decorative.

type.family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", "Noto Sans", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
type.familyMono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
type.$fontPolicy: System-ui stack only — no web fonts, inherited from the Shesha font policy. familyMono is load-bearing in this brand: IATA codes, flight numbers, booking references and fares are tabular data and align correctly only in the mono stack.

shadow.$philosophy: Skyline deliberately inverts Shesha's border-forward philosophy for CARDS ONLY. A booking, a fare quote and a boarding pass are objects that should lift off the canvas, so `card` is a real two-layer elevation rather than a whisper. Tables, inputs and dividers stay hairline-bordered exactly as Shesha specifies — do not shadow a table row. `overlay` is for genuinely floating surfaces (modals, popovers, dropdown menus).
shadow.$use: card → booking cards, fare summary panels, stat tiles. rowHover → datatable row hover only. Never stack card + overlay on the same element.

statusLifecycle.$reflist: Maps this app's four reference lists onto the five operational tones. BookingStatus: Draft→draft, Confirmed→success, Completed→success, CheckedIn→info, Cancelled→error, Refunded→info. PaymentStatus: Pending→warning, Paid→success, PartiallyPaid→warning, Refunded→info, Failed→error. FlightStatus: Scheduled→info, Boarding→warning, Departed→info, Arrived→success, Delayed→warning, Cancelled→error. CabinClass is NOT a status and must never be rendered as a status chip. Status is never colour-alone: always pair the tone with the status name.

roles.$note: sectionHeading resolves to cool near-black ink, not brand — Skyline follows Shesha in reserving the brand blue for interactive affordances, so card and section headings stay near-black. The brand blue appears as headerBandBg on page header bands, which is where an airline portal earns its identity.

$antdTheme.$use: The resolved Ant Design 6.x ConfigProvider theme for the Skyline brand. Apply this OBJECT verbatim at the app level (Configuration Studio → Settings → Default UI → Frontend → Theme settings, or the settings API with the `sha-frontend-application: default-app` header). This is the 'set once' layer and it REPAINTS THE WHOLE PORTAL — it requires explicit approval and the --allow-theme-change flag. Per-component v7 style blocks handle what it cannot express.
